purpose: Use ChartCard as the frame of a chart on a dashboard; for one box of other content use Card, and for a collection of records as cards use CardList. The box a dashboard chart lives in: a header with the title, the description and a controls zone, a content area padded or flush, an optional footer, and two optional handles that let the person move the card and resize it on a dashboard grid. The span (grid columns) and height are two-way models applied through custom properties, so the consumer's grid lays cards out with no script, and the reorder state stays with the page that owns the grid.
useWhen: Every chart on a metrics dashboard, so title, description, menu and size read the same everywhere.
A dashboard the person arranges: drag a card to reorder it, drag a corner to make it wider or taller.
avoidWhen: A KPI figure → use `stat-tile`, which is its own surface.
A general content card with no chart → use `card`.
A chart inline in a page section with its own heading → render `chart` alone.

A table, a log or a form panel on a dashboard that is not a chart → use `card` (composed in a `board` item for span and height); a grid of draggable, resizable cards → let `board` / `board-item` own the span, the height and their bounds.
related: chart`, `donut-chart` — what goes inside the content area; a chart inside a card takes its accessible name from the card title.
card` — the general-purpose card; ChartCard shares its surface tokens.
dropdown-menu` — the "More options" menu (Copy query, Export CSV) composed into the controls zone.
bestPractices: Put the aggregation tag (Sum, Average) and the variation tag in `ChartCard.Action`, before the menu.
Keep filters and the time range above the grid, never inside a card.
Use `:padded="false"` content for a plot that should run edge to edge, padded (the default) for everything else.
Give the page's grid `--chart-grid-columns` per breakpoint so a 6-column card never overflows a 1-column phone layout.
Persist `span` and `height` with the dashboard layout; they are plain numbers.
